# entire-brain P1 is clean and ready — #85 is `MERGEABLE/CLEAN`, CI 15/15

`+7,463/−57` across 33 files. Every fix is mutation-verified: revert it and its test fails.

## Bugs fixed
| | |
|---|---|
| **Silent data loss** | `distill --force` deleted sync-raised cross-member conflicts it can never regenerate |
| **Unremovable orphans** | a proposal with no fact head could be neither accepted nor rejected — stuck in every member's list forever |
| **Cross-clone resurrection** | a second clone republished conflicts the team had already settled |
| **Lost settlements** | *(mine, from the prior round)* entries were pruned even when there was nothing to mirror from |

## Performance
`Sync` already computes the post-sync head, so it returns it — **removing a full network round-trip from every hosted sync**. Plus no more needless fact-store write on a no-op reject.

## Accuracy
`facts proposals apply` now mirrors into the member's own facts immediately, instead of leaving their recall contradicting the decision they just made.

## Robustness
Three fuzz targets over the wire format, **12M+ executions**, no defects — fixed-point, struct/bytes agreement, and tamper rejection. Plus two load-sensitive brief tests de-flaked (one had failed my own verification on correct code).

## Two things I'd want you to read
**I was wrong once and reverted myself.** I read `Canonicalize`'s unknown-field pass-through as a flaw and made it reject — breaking `TestVerifyBytesToleratesUnknownFields`, which exists precisely to pin that behavior. The signature already covers unknown fields, so nothing can be smuggled or stripped, and the pass-through is what lets an older verifier validate a newer producer under ADR 0001. Behavior was right; the missing piece was a comment saying why, which I added.

**A latent trap defused:** all 10 vendored `gitmeta` files cited the *proof-of-concept* repo as upstream. That PR was superseded, not merged — the real engine is in entire-api. Anyone re-vendoring would have pulled from a dead branch. Header now records the true source, the two-way drift since, and why it's inert today (verified: local-only store, no remote, no shared ref).

## Left deliberately alone, flagged not hidden
The git-intent overlay's 500ms bound means it **also stops contributing to retrieval on a loaded machine in production** — the code shows that's a deliberate latency trade, so I didn't change product behavior uninvited.

**Remaining P1 blocker is unchanged and not in brain:** #242's wire disagreement with this client — paths, settle model, and 16-vs-64-hex proposal ids.

# PRs that must merge for P1

| # | repo | what | ready? |

# Why P1 isn't "fully verified" yet

**1. The wire mismatch is still open — I didn't fix it.**

| | #85 (client) | #242 (server) |
|---|---|---|
| path | `/brain/facts/proposals` | `/brain/proposals` |
| settle | `POST .../{id}/resolve` | `POST .../{id}/apply` + `/reject` |
| proposal id | `sha256(action,candidate,target,branch,proposedBy)` → **16 hex** | `sha256(branch,baseRef,contentRef)` → **64 hex** |

Merging both today gives you a P1 whose two halves cannot address the same proposal. I left this deliberately: which storage seam the queue gets is an architecture call, and #242's `ProposalStore.Apply` resolving server-side contradicts ADR-P1-E ("merge runs on the runner"). My recommendation — api moves to the client's shape — is written up on #242.

**2. The live round-trip has never been run.** #64 deferred it and it's still deferred. Everything on both sides is proven against fakes; the real wire has never carried a single request. That's precisely what would have caught the mismatch above.

# So, honestly
- **Fixed and ready: #85.** Bugs, performance, accuracy, fuzz coverage — done and green.
- **Not fixed: the api half.** One decision away from being mechanical work.
- **Never verified: the end-to-end path.**

=== my earlier migration ===
-- +goose Up
-- brain_fact_proposals — the OPEN PROPOSAL SET: fact-set contributions that have
-- been sealed into the brain store but have NOT yet been merged into a branch's
-- durable fact-set head (brain_fact_refs, 046).
--
-- Where brain_fact_refs is the single moving HEAD per (repo_key, branch), this table
-- is the review queue in front of it: a member (or a runner) opens a proposal naming
-- the head it merged against (base_ref) and the content-addressed facts blob it
-- produced (content_ref); a member with repo push then applies it — which performs
-- the SAME compare-and-swap the direct advance path performs, so a proposal whose
-- base_ref has been overtaken loses the CAS and is reported as a precondition
-- failure rather than silently clobbering the newer head — or rejects it.
--
-- One row per (repo_key, proposal_id). proposal_id is DETERMINISTIC — a hash over
-- (branch, base_ref, content_ref) — so re-opening the byte-identical proposal is
-- idempotent (it collides on the PK and returns the existing row) rather than
-- littering the queue with duplicates of the same contribution.
--
-- repo_key is the INJECTIVE tenancy key (slug@repo_ulid, see brainbuild.RepoKeyFor),
-- the same key brain_fact_refs (046), brain_fact_advances (047), and brain_deks (044)
-- use — never the lossy bare slug, which can collapse two distinct repos with
-- different ACLs into one keyspace.
--
-- Status is a one-way street: open → applied | rejected, and a terminal row never
-- moves again. That is enforced in the STATEMENT (every transition is an
-- `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'open'`, so a losing transition affects 0 rows and is
-- reported as a conflict) plus the CHECK constraint below, not merely by convention.
--
-- search_path is set here, not inherited: on an existing DB goose runs only this
-- migration, so 001_init's `SET search_path TO repo, public` never executes in this
-- session and a bare table name would resolve against the default path.
SET search_path TO repo, public;

CREATE TABLE brain_fact_proposals (
    repo_key        TEXT NOT NULL,
    proposal_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    branch          TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- The fact-set head the proposer merged against; '' means "merged into an empty
    -- base" (a create), exactly as in FactSetStore.Advance's oldRef.
    base_ref        TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- facts-<sha256(plaintext)> — the coordinate of the sealed proposed blob
    -- (brain/{repo_key}/facts/{content_ref}).
    content_ref     TEXT NOT NULL,
    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
    proposed_by     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    summary         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- Free-text rejection reason; '' unless status = 'rejected'.
    reason          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- The head this proposal became when applied ('' / 0 until then).
    applied_ref     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    applied_version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (repo_key, proposal_id),
    CONSTRAINT brain_fact_proposals_status_chk
        CHECK (status IN ('open', 'applied', 'rejected'))
);

-- The list endpoint reads exactly one slice: this repo's OPEN proposals, optionally
-- narrowed to a branch, oldest first. A partial index on status = 'open' keeps the
-- queue scan proportional to the open set rather than to all history.
CREATE INDEX brain_fact_proposals_open_idx
    ON brain_fact_proposals (repo_key, branch, created_at)
    WHERE status = 'open';

-- The crypto-shred-on-reject path (and the supersede-shred in brain_fact_refs's
-- advance) must ask "does any non-rejected proposal still reference this facts
-- coordinate?" before dropping its DEK — a lookup by (repo_key, content_ref) the PK
-- cannot serve.
CREATE INDEX brain_fact_proposals_content_ref_idx
    ON brain_fact_proposals (repo_key, content_ref);

-- Grant exactly what the queue needs — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE — and deliberately NO
-- DELETE: a resolved proposal is retained as the record of who contributed what and
-- what happened to it. Stating the grant explicitly (rather than leaning on 001's
-- schema default privileges) makes the "no DELETE" design visible at the table's
-- birth, matching brain_deks (044), brain_overlay_branches (045), and
-- brain_fact_refs (046).
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_fact_proposals TO repo_rw;

-- Debug-readable view matching the *_readable convention: a proposal row is refs +
-- status + attribution, no secret material (the proposed facts themselves live
-- encrypted in the object store under content_ref), so expose every column.
CREATE VIEW brain_fact_proposals_readable AS
    SELECT repo_key, proposal_id, branch, base_ref, content_ref, status, proposed_by,
           summary, reason, applied_ref, applied_version, created_at, updated_at
    FROM brain_fact_proposals;

-- +goose Down
SET search_path TO repo, public;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS brain_fact_proposals_readable;
REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_fact_proposals FROM repo_rw;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS brain_fact_proposals;

git rm -q internal/store/migrations/repo/20260802142559_brain_fact_proposals.sql
NEW=internal/store/migrations/repo/20260817120000_brain_proposal_refs.sql
cat > "$NEW" <<'EOF'
-- +goose Up
-- brain_proposal_refs — the moving HEAD of a branch's OPEN PROPOSAL SET.
--
-- The open proposal set is a single content-addressed blob (the JSON array of open
-- proposals), pointed at by one compare-and-swapped ref per (repo_key, branch) — the
-- exact shape brain_fact_refs (046) gives the fact-set head, and stored through the
-- same encrypting blob store. It is deliberately NOT a row-per-proposal queue:
--
--   ADR-P1-E puts the merge on the runner. The runner reads the fact head and the
--   open set, computes the resolution locally, and compare-and-swaps BOTH back under
--   the refs it read. A server that stored proposals as rows would have to re-derive
--   which entries survive a resolution — that is merge logic, and a second
--   implementation of it is exactly the divergence the wire contract exists to stop.
--   As a blob the server never interprets the contents: it swaps a pointer.
--
--   It also keeps proposal identity single-sourced. Ids are derived by the client
--   from the proposal's own fields; a server-side id derived from storage
--   coordinates would disagree, and no proposal could be addressed across the wire.
--
-- repo_key is the INJECTIVE tenancy key (slug@repo_ulid, see brainbuild.RepoKeyFor),
-- the same key brain_fact_refs (046), brain_fact_advances (047) and brain_deks (044)
-- use — never the lossy bare slug, which can collapse two repos with different ACLs
-- into one keyspace.
--
-- search_path is set here, not inherited: on an existing DB goose runs only this
-- migration, so 001_init's `SET search_path TO repo, public` never executes in this
-- session and a bare table name would resolve against the default path.
SET search_path TO repo, public;

CREATE TABLE brain_proposal_refs (
    repo_key    TEXT NOT NULL,
    branch      TEXT NOT NULL,
    current_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    version     BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (repo_key, branch)
);

-- Mirrors brain_fact_refs_current_ref_idx: the shred-on-supersede path counts, after
-- moving a branch off oldRef, whether any branch still references it — a scan by
-- (repo_key, current_ref) that the PK (leading repo_key, branch) cannot serve.
CREATE INDEX brain_proposal_refs_current_ref_idx ON brain_proposal_refs (repo_key, current_ref);

-- SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and deliberately NO DELETE: a head only ever moves, it is
-- never removed. Stated explicitly rather than leaning on 001's schema defaults, so
-- the "no DELETE" design is visible at the table's birth, matching 044/045/046.
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_proposal_refs TO repo_rw;

-- Debug-readable view per the *_readable convention: a head is a content ref plus a
-- version, carrying no secret material (the proposals themselves live encrypted in
-- the object store under current_ref), so expose every column.
CREATE VIEW brain_proposal_refs_readable AS
    SELECT repo_key, branch, current_ref, version, updated_at
    FROM brain_proposal_refs;

-- +goose Down
SET search_path TO repo, public;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS brain_proposal_refs_readable;
REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_proposal_refs FROM repo_rw;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS brain_proposal_refs;
EOF

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/p0p1/api-242
go build ./... 2>&1|head -2

git add -A internal/ 
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(brain): serve the open proposal set on the contract the client speaks

The two halves of P1 were built independently and disagreed on the wire in three
ways at once, so no proposal could be addressed across it: the paths differed
(/brain/proposals vs the client's /brain/facts/proposals), the settle verb differed
(apply + reject vs one resolve), and proposal identity differed outright — this side
derived it from storage coordinates as 64 hex, the client derives it from the
proposal's own fields as 16. Every unit test on both sides passed regardless, because
nothing exercised the boundary.

This side moves, for three reasons. ADR-P1-E puts the merge on the runner, and
ProposalStore.Apply re-derived resolutions server-side — a second implementation of
merge logic, which is the divergence the wire contract exists to prevent. The client
already addresses the queue under the fact-set family, where it belongs: the open set
IS the fact set's review queue, and this service already serves /brain/facts and
/brain/facts/advance. And identity has to be single-sourced; only the client can
derive it, since only the client knows the proposal's fields.

The queue is now one compare-and-swapped blob per branch instead of a row per
proposal. The server never interprets an entry — it stores bytes and moves pointers —
so a newer client can add proposal fields with no server change. That reuses the
fact-set machinery wholesale: the same read-CAS-write store over its own ref index
(brain_proposal_refs) and its own blob kind, so the two heads move and are
crypto-shredded independently. KindProposals exists precisely because sharing
KindFacts would let the fact-head shred drop a live proposal blob's DEK, since no
fact head references a proposal coordinate.

resolve swaps both heads from the refs the runner read, facts first: losing the set
CAS after advancing facts leaves the entry queued and the runner re-resolves
idempotently, whereas the reverse order could drop the entry while the facts never
moved, losing the settlement. factsUnchanged settles the set alone, which is the only
way an orphaned proposal — one whose facts are gone entirely — ever leaves the queue;
it is refused with accept, where skipping the fact write would retire the proposal and
silently drop its merge result.

The row-queue table is replaced rather than migrated: #242 has not merged, so its
migration never shipped.

Adds a wire-contract test fed the client's literal JSON. The two repos cannot import
each other, so nothing else makes a rename or a retyped field fail a build — which is
how three incompatibilities survived this long.
EOF

entire-api answers 503 whenever the hosted brain is disabled — the same way its
fact-set endpoints do — but the client only treated 404 and 501 as an absent queue, so
a deployment with the brain switched off surfaced as an unexpected-status error
instead of degrading. That failed a sync whose facts had already landed.

Read it as unsupported on both the list and publish paths, so the proposals stay in
the local review queue with a warning. A genuinely transient 503 costs one cycle: the
next sync re-checks and publishes then.

Found by diffing this client against the server it talks to rather than by running it;
the two live in different repos, so no test on either side covered the boundary.
